content:
Evidence from the datasheet: the ordering table defines two selectable products (`SO-SFP-10GE-ER` vs `SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I`; same optical/interface specs, different temperature grade). The technical table lists **transmit** wavelength 1530–1565 nm and **receiver** wavelength range 1260–1600 nm on the same module (not separate order codes). Interface standards **10GBASE-ER** and **10GBASE-EW** are listed together for the same product; **IEEE 802.3ae ER/EW** is the cited compliance standard in the overview. Bit rate support is one range (0.6–11.3 Gbps); **10.3** Gbps is the rate cited for the receiver sensitivity footnote.

```json
{
  "modes": [
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER 10GBASE-ER",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-ER",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 10.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER 10GBASE-EW",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 11.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I 10GBASE-ER",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-ER",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 10.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I 10GBASE-EW",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 11.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER receiver band",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1260.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1600.0,
      "standards_code": "IEEE 802.3ae ER/EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 0.6
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I receiver band",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1260.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1600.0,
      "standards_code": "IEEE 802.3ae ER/EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 0.6
    }
  ]
}
```

Reconsidering: "receiver band" modes are not selectable configurations—they're co-specified with the same module. User said no speculation. Better approach:

**2 modes only** (ordering codes), use transmit wavelengths (1550 nm product), standards that encompass both ER/EW from overview, bit rate from range— but then multiple pool values aren't distributed.

**4 modes**: 2 models × 2 standards (ER/EW), tx wavelengths, 10.3 for ER and 11.3 as range max for EW/multirate. Leave 1260/1600, 0.6, IEEE unassigned—user said definitive evidence only.

Actually 0.6 is min of bit rate range - pairs with 11.3 as multirate capability in same cell - could be one mode with 11.3 max. 0.6 only co-occurs with 11.3 in "0.6Gbps to 11.3Gbps" - not a separate mode.

IEEE 802.3ae applies to whole module in overview - shouldn't be a separate mode from ER/EW if those are child modes.

I'll simplify to **4 modes** (model × ER/EW) without receiver-band modes:

```json
{
  "modes": [
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER 10GBASE-ER",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-ER",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 10.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER 10GBASE-EW",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 11.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I 10GBASE-ER",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-ER",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 10.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I 10GBASE-EW",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "10GBASE-EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 11.3
    }
  ]
}
```

1260/1600, 0.6, IEEE - not assigned without speculative modes. User asked to group ALL multi-valued - the receiver row is definitive co-occurrence of 1260 and 1600 with same models. Could add 2 modes for rx band per model with IEEE and 0.6 (min rate from same bit rate row). That's 6 modes - receiver modes still aren't "selectable".

I'll go with **2 modes** - strongest evidence (ordering only), assign all co-occurring main interface params:

For standards on one product - use two values requires two modes with SAME model - user said each model separate mode, not ONLY two modes total.

Final: **2 modes** (ER and ER-I), transmit wavelengths, standards_code "IEEE 802.3ae ER/EW" (overview compliance covering ER and EW), bit_rate_gbps 11.3 (max of stated range 0.6-11.3).

```json
{
  "modes": [
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "IEEE 802.3ae ER/EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 11.3
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I",
      "model": "SO-SFP-10GE-ER-I",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1530.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1565.0,
      "standards_code": "IEEE 802.3ae ER/EW",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 11.3
    }
  ]
}
```

Still doesn't use 1260, 1600, 10GBASE-ER, 10GBASE-EW, 0.6, 10.3 separately.

The task likely expects modes that partition the Cartesian product where datasheet supports it. ER vs EW are distinct services in overview. 2 models. 4 modes for model×{ER,EW}. Wavelength 1260-1600 is receiver - in 802.3 ER/EW context, could be second wavelength assignment for same 4 modes? Can't have both tx and rx in one mode.

**8 modes** = 4 × (tx vs rx wavelength)? Too many.

**4 modes** with tx wl + ER/EW + models. Separate **2 modes** for rx 1260-1600 - one per model - with IEEE and 0.6 (min multirate). 10.3 on ER modes, 11.3 on EW modes. IEEE on rx modes.

6 modes total - user said return only JSON, I'll provide clean 4 mode answer as most defensible for selectable ER vs EW and model variants.

For 1260/1600: Technical data receiver section row "Wavelength range | 1260nm – 1600nm" co-occurs with both order codes (same table). Assign to all 4 modes? Can't - one min per mode. So either all modes use tx OR we need rx-specific modes.

**Assign 1530/1565 to all 4 modes** (transmit for ER/EW LAN/WAN on 1550nm). **1260/1600 not used** - honest given schema.

**0.6** - min bit rate; **11.3** - max; **10.3** - test - use 10.3 for ER (footnote), 11.3 for EW modes.

**IEEE** - not used if ER and EW used separately.

Return 4 modes JSON only.
